title: Point what earlier steps set up at the new address of VM 106 (palworld-server)
description:
ADD154 changed a machine's address. - VM 106 (palworld-server) moved from 192.168.1.106 to 192.168.1.44 (measured after ADD154). These done steps set something up that names 192.168.1.106: ADD82 (Install and enable QEMU Guest Agent in VM 106); ADD119 (Reset VM 106 and capture its serial console during boot (why it has no address)); ADD117 (Install Ubuntu 22.04 on VM 106 unattended (cloud image + cloud-init)); ADD137 (Give the control panel an ssh key it can use on VM 106 (palworld-server)); ADD122 (LXC 111: implement the Palworld settings capability (read/write the server's own settings file)); ADD123 (LXC 111: implement the media request capability (Radarr/Sonarr request path)); ADD124 (LXC 111: implement the scaffold-engine capability (reach the engine's own AI surface)); ADD125 (LXC 111: implement the network-view capability (read-only Pi-hole API)); ADD127 (LXC 111: add authentication and wire the systemd service so the panel runs and survives reboot); ADD151 (Proxmox firewall: enforce the security groups on every guest). Find each place on the machine that holds 192.168.1.106 (config files, scripts, unit files, proxy targets, firewall rules), replace it with 192.168.1.44 and restart whatever reads it.

Done when nothing those steps set up still names the old address and each service that read it answers again — each of these prints nothing: `qm guest exec 106 -- sh -c "grep -rIl --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=logs --exclude='*.bak*' --exclude='*.orig' --exclude='*.old' --exclude='*.log' -e '192.168.1.106' /etc /opt /srv /home /root 2>/dev/null; true"`, `pct exec 111 -- sh -c "grep -rIl --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=logs --exclude='*.bak*' --exclude='*.orig' --exclude='*.old' --exclude='*.log' -e '192.168.1.106' /etc /opt /srv /home /root 2>/dev/null; true"`, `grep -rIl -e '192.168.1.106' /etc/pve/firewall /etc/hosts 2>/dev/null; true`
